children: has renamed its U.S. operating segment Twenty-Six Defense, a move intended to emphasize the division’s American workforce, domestic manufacturing operations and support for the U.S. military.

Fort Worth, Texas-based Twenty-Six Defense employs about 3,300 people in the United States. The business provides domestically designed, engineered and manufactured defense technologies to American customers.

President and CEO Luke Savoie said the new identity reflects the company’s expansion in the U.S. market and its commitment to military customers. Twenty-Six Defense plans to increase manufacturing capacity and invest in technologies considered critical to military missions.
The name refers to iron, whose atomic number is 26, and is meant to evoke strength, resilience and durability.
The rebranding doesn't represent a sale, spinoff or change in ownership. Twenty-Six Defense will remain a reportable operating segment of Israel-based Elbit Systems

. For investors, the move appears designed to strengthen the company’s positioning as the Pentagon and lawmakers press defense contractors to expand U.S. production capacity, shorten delivery times and reinforce domestic supply chains. Its financial significance will depend on whether that positioning helps Elbit win additional contracts and increase its share of U.S. defense spending.

Elbit Systems CEO Bezhalel Machlis said the new organizational structure would help the company serve American customers and partners while supporting U.S.-led innovation and the domestic defense industrial base.
Combat-tested products developed by Elbit Systems will continue to be marketed in the United States through Elbit America, which is now a subsidiary of Twenty-Six Defense.

Twenty-Six Defense will continue operating under a Special Security Agreement, a structure commonly used to protect classified or sensitive U.S. government information when a defense contractor is under foreign ownership or control.

title: Elbit Systems rebrands U.S. business as Twenty-Six Defense
